title: Final density answer
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be ρ = ρ₀/8.

title: Final energy answer
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must be ΔE_k = -(2/3)Gπρ₀ m r₀².

title: Mass conservation reasoning
description: Important: The student must apply mass conservation within a co-moving volume to relate densities at different radii.

title: Shell theorem application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the shell theorem to equate the gravitational force to that from the enclosed mass at the center.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important: The student must set up the energy conservation equation using the given gravitational potential energy formula.

title: Hubble constant trend
description: Important: The student must conclude that H decreases with increasing time t, based on the sign of ΔE_k and the universe's expansion.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The student's work shows consistent units throughout the derivation, especially in the energy expression.

title: Sign error in energy
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly calculates a positive ΔE_k, missing that kinetic energy decreases as the body moves away.

title: Incorrect mass scaling
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly scales mass or density, e.g., using ρ ∝ 1/r² instead of ρ ∝ 1/r³.
